narrativeReportMd:
# CompartmentDefinition R4→R6 breaking-change assessment

## Bottom line
`CompartmentDefinition` keeps the same canonical identity, base, and resource type, but R6 introduces material local model changes. The most concrete R4→R6 break is removal of `CompartmentDefinition.resource.documentation`; the largest bidirectional migration issue is the required `resource.code` binding moving from the R4 resource-type universe to the R6 resource-type universe. R6 also adds `versionAlgorithm[x]`, `title`, `resource.startParam`, and `resource.endParam`, which creates R6→R4 information loss.

## Scope
The assessment covers `CompartmentDefinition`'s own StructureDefinition elements, local constraints, local bindings, and directly related local terminology. Inherited `Resource`, `DomainResource`, `Element`, `Extension`, and `BackboneElement` deltas are not reported as local findings.

## Main migration themes
The main migration work is not a wholesale resource rename: it is handling one removed nested documentation field, updating generated models for new optional fields, and planning conversions for required-code bindings whose value sets track the R6 resource and compartment universe. Systems that use CompartmentDefinition for access-control compartment membership should pay special attention to the R6 clarification that `resource.param` names are based on HL7 core SearchParameter codes, not server-specific aliases.

## Highest-impact findings
High-impact findings are `CompartmentDefinition.resource.code` value-set churn and the semantic clarification of `CompartmentDefinition.resource.param`. The former can make R4 CompartmentDefinition instances invalid in R6 when they list resource types removed or renamed in the R6 ballot, and can make R6 definitions unrepresentable in R4 when they list newly added R6 resource types. The latter can change runtime compartment membership calculations even though the element shape is unchanged.

## Findings requiring human review
Human review is recommended for resource-type mappings, new `$everything` start/end parameter semantics, the widened compartment-type binding, and runtime compartment-membership interpretation. The R6 package also contains `CompartmentDefinition-group.json` with `code: "Group"`, while the inspected R6 `compartment-type` CodeSystem contains `Patient`, `Encounter`, `RelatedPerson`, `Practitioner`, `Device`, and `EpisodeOfCare` but not `Group`; that ballot-package inconsistency should be resolved before treating the required binding as final.

## Backward-compatible design observations
Most R6 additions could have been represented in R4 with extensions, and the removed `resource.documentation` element could have been retained as deprecated to preserve old instances. The resource-type and compartment-type binding changes are largely driven by the FHIR version's resource inventory and compartment model, so a completely backward-compatible base-resource design would have been difficult, but ConceptMaps or cross-version extensions would reduce conversion loss.

## Follow-up analysis
Separate reports should own inherited base-resource changes, detailed resource additions/removals, the resource-type and compartment-type terminology artifacts, and `$everything` OperationDefinition/SearchParameter semantics.

summary.executiveSummaryMd: `CompartmentDefinition` has local R4→R6 breaking changes, chiefly removal of `resource.documentation` and required binding changes for `resource.code`. The top migration concerns are resource-type code churn, R6-only `$everything` start/end parameter metadata, and runtime interpretation of `resource.param`. Confidence is high for the computable diffs, with uncertainty around ballot intent and the observed R6 `Group` compartment inconsistency.
summary.migrationThemesMd: Migrations should combine structural transforms and terminology/version-aware validation. R4→R6 transforms need to drop or preserve `resource.documentation` out of band and review all `resource.code` values against the R6 resource-type ValueSet. R6→R4 transforms need extension or sidecar strategies for `title`, `versionAlgorithm[x]`, `resource.startParam`, and `resource.endParam`, and must decide how to handle R6-only compartment and resource codes.
summary.confidenceSummaryMd: Confidence is high for element presence, cardinality, type, local constraint, and local binding comparisons because both primary StructureDefinitions and relevant local terminology artifacts were present. Confidence is lower for rationale and operational impact because no official diff/JIRA notes or full narrative-page comparison were supplied, and the R6 ballot package appears internally inconsistent about a `Group` compartment code.

findings.title: CompartmentDefinition.resource.documentation was removed

oldState.summary: Optional nested string documentation was available on each resource relationship row.

semanticText.short: Additional documentation about the resource and compartment
semanticText.definition: Additional documentation about the resource and compartment.

oldState.narrativeMd: In R4, each `CompartmentDefinition.resource` entry could carry `documentation` as a `0..1` string.

newState.summary: No corresponding R6 element is present.
newState.narrativeMd: The R6 snapshot and differential have no `CompartmentDefinition.resource.documentation` element. No direct replacement field is present in the same backbone.

facts.note: Absent from the R6 snapshot and differential.

structuredDelta.matchingRationaleMd: The parent backbone and neighboring elements `resource.code` and `resource.param` persist; only `resource.documentation` is absent in R6, so this is a removal rather than a rename.

impact.impactRationaleMd: This is a direct validation break for R4 instances that populate `resource.documentation`: strict R6 validation will treat the property as unknown content because the element no longer exists. The affected element is optional and appears rare in core R4 compartment definitions, but the R4 package example does use it.
impact.safetyOrBusinessRiskMd: Loss is mainly explanatory metadata about compartment/resource relationships. It can still matter for generated documentation or human review of access-control definitions.

justification.inferredGoal: Simplify the resource relationship backbone and rely on computable parameters plus narrative/spec documentation rather than per-row string documentation.
justification.backwardCompatibleAlternativeSummary: Retain `resource.documentation` as a deprecated optional string with clarified non-normative semantics.
justification.justificationRationaleMd: The inferred goal of simplifying the resource backbone is reasonable, but removing an optional, non-modifier string creates a direct old-valid/new-invalid break. Retaining the field while marking it deprecated would have preserved R4 instances and still allowed R6 implementations to discourage or ignore new use.
justification.backwardCompatibleAlternativeMd: The best less-breaking base R6 design would keep `CompartmentDefinition.resource.documentation` at `0..1 string`, label it deprecated or legacy, and clarify that authoritative guidance belongs in narrative or implementation documentation. That avoids data loss for existing instances with low long-term burden, though the legacy element could remain visible indefinitely.
justification.alternativeTradeoffSummary: Compatibility cost is carrying a legacy documentation field; the tradeoff is modest because there is no competing R6 same-resource replacement.

evidence.detail: R4 defines `resource.documentation` as 0..1 string.
R6 has no `CompartmentDefinition.resource.documentation` element.
The R4 package example uses the removed element, showing at least one local instance pattern affected.
evidence.quote: The device used as the message sender and recipient

resource.documentation: The device used as the message sender and recipient

examples.examplesMd: The example focuses on the removed element. A lossless migration would need to carry the documentation in an extension, external documentation, or a sidecar mapping because R6 has no direct replacement element.

findings.narrativeMd: `CompartmentDefinition.resource.documentation` was removed from the `resource` backbone. Any R4 CompartmentDefinition instance that documented why a resource belonged to a compartment in this field will fail strict R6 structural validation unless the content is dropped or moved elsewhere.
findings.validationAndCompatibilityMd: R4-valid instances with `resource.documentation` become R6-invalid because the element is no longer part of the content model. This does not create an R6→R4 problem because R6 has no such element. Runtime risk is mostly for generated models, serializers, and documentation tooling that expect the field.
findings.migrationGuidanceMd: Inventory all R4 CompartmentDefinition instances for `resource.documentation`. If the text is needed, map it to an implementation-defined extension or external documentation before R6 validation; otherwise drop it intentionally and document the loss. Add tests with and without `documentation` to ensure unknown-property handling is explicit.
findings.backwardCompatibilityAnalysisMd: The removal was avoidable from a wire-compatibility standpoint because the element was optional, non-modifier, and non-summary. Deprecating it would have preserved existing instances while still discouraging new use.

facts.oldValue: R4 core CompartmentDefinition instances generally list 145 resource rows
facts.newValue: R6 core CompartmentDefinition instances generally list 126 resource rows

structuredDelta.matchingRationaleMd: The same element id and path persist with unchanged cardinality and type; the material change is the versioned required ValueSet and the underlying resource-code universe.

impact.impactRationaleMd: Because the binding remains `required`, resource-type code churn is a validation issue, not just documentation. An R4 CompartmentDefinition row whose `resource.code` names a resource type absent from the R6 value set is invalid in R6; conversely, R6 rows for newly introduced resource types cannot validate as R4. Generated enum types and switch statements over resource names also need updates.
impact.safetyOrBusinessRiskMd: Compartment definitions commonly drive server compartment search and access-control behavior. Incorrectly dropping or mis-mapping resource rows can over- or under-include resources in a compartment.

justification.inferredGoal: Align compartment resource rows with the resource types available in the target FHIR release.
justification.backwardCompatibleAlternativeSummary: Broaden the R6 base binding to include deprecated R4 resource-type codes or an explicit legacy-code branch.
justification.justificationRationaleMd: The goal of making `resource.code` describe the resource inventory of the target FHIR release is central to CompartmentDefinition conformance. A less-breaking union binding is technically possible, but it would materially weaken validation by permitting compartment rows whose resource types have been removed, renamed, or replaced in R6.
justification.backwardCompatibleAlternativeMd: A partial base-design alternative would include legacy R4 resource codes in the R6 value set as deprecated compatibility concepts, or add a distinct legacy-code representation for cross-version rows. That is more than migration guidance, but it creates duplicate or stale representations of the same compartment-resource fact, complicates generated enums and switch logic, and risks obsolete resource rows never disappearing.
justification.alternativeTradeoffSummary: Preserving old codes would keep more R4 instances valid but would allow rows for resources no longer present in R6 and accumulate obsolete enum values.

evidence.detail: R4 required binding is `ValueSet/resource-types|4.0.1`.
R6 required binding is `ValueSet/resource-types|6.0.0-ballot4`.
Local comparison found 41 R4 codes not present in the R6 value set and 20 R6 codes not present in the R4 value set.

examples.examplesMd: `DocumentManifest` is in the local R4 resource-types comparison but not in the R6 value set; `ActorDefinition` is in the R6 value set but not R4. Actual mappings depend on the global resource migration strategy.

findings.narrativeMd: `CompartmentDefinition.resource.code` still has the same path, cardinality, and primitive type, but its required value set now represents the R6 ballot resource inventory. That makes the element a focal point for cross-version failures: rows for resource types removed, renamed, or consolidated after R4 will no longer validate in R6, and rows for newly introduced R6 resources cannot be represented as valid R4.
findings.validationAndCompatibilityMd: This is hard instance-breaking for any R4 instance containing a now-absent resource-type code, because required binding validation rejects the value. It is also a high R6→R4 representability risk for newly introduced R6 resource codes. Runtime code generators that materialize resource type enums will see both removed and added enum members.
findings.migrationGuidanceMd: Build a version-aware mapping table for every `resource.code` value before validating migrated instances. Some rows may be dropped because the resource no longer exists; others may map to renamed or replacement resources; some require manual review. Preserve the original code in an extension or audit log when the mapping is lossy, and test both official core CompartmentDefinition instances and local custom definitions.
findings.backwardCompatibilityAnalysisMd: The change is largely tied to the FHIR version's resource inventory, so a fully backward-compatible R6 required binding would be misleading. However, explicit cross-version ConceptMaps or a standard extension carrying the prior release's resource code would reduce migration ambiguity.
findings.reviewerNotesMd: The detailed semantics of each added/removed resource code should be owned by the corresponding resource or terminology reports. This finding only covers the local consequence of the required binding on CompartmentDefinition instances.

findings.title: R6 adds resource.startParam and resource.endParam for $everything date-window interpretation

oldState.summary: No R4 elements identify search parameters for `$everything.start` or `$everything.end`.
oldState.narrativeMd: R4 CompartmentDefinition resource rows could list compartment membership parameters but had no dedicated start/end date-window metadata.

newState.summary: R6 adds optional `startParam` and `endParam`, both `0..1 uri`, on each resource row.
newState.narrativeMd: R6 can say which search parameter maps requests made with `$everything.start` and `$everything.end` for a resource row.

facts.newValue: Most non-example R6 CompartmentDefinition instances populate 58 startParam and 58 endParam values.

structuredDelta.matchingRationaleMd: These are new sibling elements under the retained `resource` backbone; no R4 element had the same cardinality/type/semantics.

impact.impactRationaleMd: Adding optional fields does not invalidate R4 instances when moving forward. It is a high R6→R4 risk because R4 has nowhere to carry the operational mapping for `$everything.start` and `$everything.end`, and the local R6 package uses these fields extensively in core compartment definitions.
impact.safetyOrBusinessRiskMd: Incorrect or lost date-window mappings can change which resources a server returns for compartment-level `$everything` operations.

justification.inferredGoal: Make `$everything` date-window behavior computable per resource type in a compartment.
justification.backwardCompatibleAlternativeSummary: Not applicable; these are optional R6 additions that preserve R4 instances rather than an R4-to-R6 base-design break.
justification.justificationRationaleMd: The inferred goal of making `$everything` date-window behavior computable per compartment resource row is reasonable, and adding optional fields does not invalidate R4 CompartmentDefinition instances. The compatibility issue is backward conversion from richer R6 content, not an avoidable forward break.
justification.backwardCompatibleAlternativeMd: No backward-compatible alternative is applicable under the calibration rules because the R6 base resource only adds optional content. R4 extensions could preserve `startParam` and `endParam` during down-conversion, but such backports do not show that the R6 base design should have avoided first-class optional elements.
justification.alternativeTradeoffSummary: R6-to-R4 round-tripping may need extensions or sidecar metadata, but that is a conversion mitigation rather than a less-breaking R6 base design.

evidence.detail: R6 defines `startParam` as 0..1 uri for `$everything.start` mapping.
R6 defines `endParam` as 0..1 uri for `$everything.end` mapping.
R4 has no `startParam` or `endParam` elements.
The R6 package core compartment definitions populate these fields widely, with samples such as Account.period, AdverseEvent.occurrence, and Appointment.date.

examples.examplesMd: The migration example uses placeholder extension URLs. A production transform should use agreed cross-version extensions if available.

findings.narrativeMd: R6 adds computable start/end search-parameter metadata to each compartment resource row. This is not an R4→R6 validation break, but it is a major round-trip concern because R4 cannot express the fields and R6 core artifacts actively use them for `$everything` behavior.
findings.validationAndCompatibilityMd: R4 instances remain structurally acceptable with respect to these additions. R6 instances containing `startParam` or `endParam` are not cleanly representable in R4 unless the information is moved to extensions or out-of-band metadata. Generated R6 models will also have new properties that R4 models lack.
findings.migrationGuidanceMd: For R6→R4 conversion, decide whether `$everything` date-window behavior must be preserved. If yes, map `startParam` and `endParam` to extensions or a sidecar configuration and ensure runtime code reads that preserved metadata. If no, document the loss and test `$everything` queries around date filters.
findings.backwardCompatibilityAnalysisMd: First-class R6 elements are justified for computable interoperability, but cross-version compatibility would be better with standardized extensions usable in R4. The tradeoff is that extensions require profiles and explicit runtime support.

justification.inferredGoal: Define additional compartment categories in the R6 compartment model.
justification.backwardCompatibleAlternativeSummary: Not applicable; widening the required compartment-type code set preserves all R4 compartment codes.
justification.justificationRationaleMd: If R6 defines additional core compartment categories, adding them to the required compartment-type binding is a reasonable base conformance change. Existing R4 codes remain valid in R6; the main uncertainty is the ballot package inconsistency around a `Group` compartment instance.

Local R6 CodeSystem has six concepts and adds `EpisodeOfCare` compared with R4.

examples.examplesMd: An R6 `EpisodeOfCare` compartment definition cannot validate as R4 because R4's required binding lacks that code.

findings.narrativeMd: `CompartmentDefinition.code` remains mandatory, but the required code set widened. This does not break existing R4 compartment definitions that use Patient, Encounter, RelatedPerson, Practitioner, or Device, but it breaks backward conversion for R6 definitions that use the new code.
findings.validationAndCompatibilityMd: No old-valid/new-invalid issue was found for the five R4 codes. R6-valid `EpisodeOfCare` content is not R4-representable under the required binding. Implementations with generated compartment-type enums must add the new code and audit default branches.
findings.migrationGuidanceMd: For R6→R4, either reject new compartment types, map them to extensions or out-of-band configuration, or define a profile-specific compatibility policy. Review the R6 ballot package's `Group` compartment inconsistency before finalizing enum handling.
findings.backwardCompatibilityAnalysisMd: Adding the code to the base value set is probably necessary if the core R6 spec defines the compartment. A profile or extension would have been more backward-compatible but less interoperable as a base compartment definition.
findings.reviewerNotesMd: Human review should verify whether `Group` is intentionally a new compartment type omitted from the inspected CodeSystem, or a ballot packaging defect.

findings.title: R6 adds top-level title and versionAlgorithm[x] metadata

oldState.summary: R4 CompartmentDefinition had no `title` or `versionAlgorithm[x]` elements.
oldState.narrativeMd: R4 supported `url`, `version`, and `name`, but not a human-friendly title or computable version comparison algorithm on this resource.

newState.summary: R6 adds optional `title` and optional choice `versionAlgorithm[x]` (`string` or `Coding`).
newState.narrativeMd: `title` is a human-friendly name; `versionAlgorithm[x]` describes how to compare business versions and can be a FHIRPath string or Coding.

structuredDelta.matchingRationaleMd: Both elements are present in the R6 differential and absent from the R4 snapshot/differential.

impact.impactRationaleMd: Optional additions do not invalidate R4 instances. They do create generated-model and conversion differences: R6 serializers can emit fields R4 parsers do not know, and R4 has no native place for version comparison logic.
impact.safetyOrBusinessRiskMd: Loss of version comparison logic can affect artifact selection or dependency resolution, but not clinical data content directly.

justification.inferredGoal: Align CompartmentDefinition with richer canonical-resource metadata patterns.
justification.backwardCompatibleAlternativeSummary: Not applicable; optional `title` and `versionAlgorithm[x]` additions do not make R4 instances invalid in R6.
justification.justificationRationaleMd: The goal of aligning CompartmentDefinition with richer canonical-resource metadata is reasonable, and the additions are optional. The reported incompatibility is that R6 instances may carry metadata that R4 cannot natively represent, not that R4-valid instances fail in R6.
justification.backwardCompatibleAlternativeMd: No backward-compatible base-design alternative is applicable for the forward R4-to-R6 assessment. Cross-version extensions for `title` or `versionAlgorithm[x]` are useful preservation mechanisms when converting R6 content back to R4, but they do not count as alternatives to adding optional first-class R6 elements.
justification.alternativeTradeoffSummary: R4 extension strategies can reduce down-conversion loss but are not less-breaking alternatives to optional R6 base metadata.

evidence.detail: R6 adds `title` as 0..1 string.
R6 adds `versionAlgorithm[x]` as 0..1 string or Coding with extensible binding.
R4 has no corresponding elements.

examples.examplesMd: R4 has no native `title` or `versionAlgorithm[x]`; preserving either requires extensions or sidecar metadata.

findings.narrativeMd: R6 adds optional canonical metadata fields to CompartmentDefinition. The most technically significant is `versionAlgorithm[x]`, a new choice element that changes generated classes and can affect artifact-version comparison.
findings.validationAndCompatibilityMd: R4 instances are not invalidated. R6 instances containing these fields cannot be represented as pure R4 JSON/XML without information loss or extensions. Choice-element code generators must create `versionAlgorithmString` and `versionAlgorithmCoding` accessors or equivalents.
findings.migrationGuidanceMd: For R6→R4, preserve `title` and `versionAlgorithm[x]` in extensions if round-trip fidelity or artifact dependency resolution matters. Add parser tests for both string and Coding forms of `versionAlgorithm[x]`.
findings.backwardCompatibilityAnalysisMd: The additions are not disruptive for forward migration, but first-class R6 elements are not backward-compatible on the wire. Standard cross-version extensions would reduce round-trip loss.

findings.title: Warning-level canonical constraints were added or tightened for name and url

oldState.summary: R4 had warning `cpd-0` for machine-friendly names and no local URL character warning.

constraints.human: Name should be usable as an identifier for the module by machine processing applications such as code generation

oldState.narrativeMd: The R4 root warning allowed a single initial capital followed by zero to 254 alphanumeric/underscore characters. `url` had no equivalent local warning forbidding `|` or `#`.

newState.summary: R6 has warning `cnl-0` with an anchored name regex and warning `cnl-1` forbidding problematic canonical URL characters.

constraints.human: Name should be usable as an identifier for the module by machine processing applications such as code generation
URL should not contain | or # - these characters make processing canonical references problematic

newState.narrativeMd: R6 renames and tightens the name warning and adds a URL warning intended to avoid canonical-reference parsing problems.

structuredDelta.matchingRationaleMd: `cpd-0` and `cnl-0` have the same human intent but different keys and expressions; `cnl-1` is a new local URL warning.

impact.impactRationaleMd: Both constraints are warnings, so ordinary FHIR validation should not reject instances solely because they fail them. However, CI pipelines and publication tooling that treat warnings as errors may start failing for short or poorly formed canonical names/URLs.

justification.inferredGoal: Improve canonical artifact hygiene and code-generation safety.
justification.backwardCompatibleAlternativeSummary: Keep the R4 warning key/expression and make the stricter URL/name hygiene guidance non-invariant or opt-in.
justification.justificationRationaleMd: The goal of improving machine-friendly names and canonical URLs is reasonable, and the constraints are warnings rather than fatal validity rules. A less-disruptive route exists, but it would not provide the same standard validator signal for problematic canonical values.
justification.backwardCompatibleAlternativeMd: A partial less-breaking base design would preserve the old `cpd-0` warning behavior and move the stricter `cnl-0`/`cnl-1` checks to narrative guidance, publication tooling, or an opt-in best-practice profile. That would help warning-as-error pipelines and existing suppressions, but at the cost of less consistent R6 validation feedback for URL separators, spaces, and nonconforming artifact names.
justification.alternativeTradeoffSummary: This would reduce warning-as-error disruption but would also weaken uniform automated feedback for canonical-reference hygiene.

evidence.detail: R4 root name warning uses `cpd-0` and the looser expression.
R6 root name warning uses `cnl-0` and an anchored expression requiring at least one trailing character after the initial capital.
R6 adds a warning that URL should not contain `|`, `#`, or spaces.

examples.examplesMd: A one-character `name` such as `A`, or a canonical `url` containing `#`, is not necessarily invalid from these constraints alone, but R6 validation can emit warnings where R4 did not.

findings.narrativeMd: R6 strengthens validation guidance around canonical names and URLs. The rules are warnings rather than errors, but they are visible to validators and publication tooling.
findings.validationAndCompatibilityMd: This is not a hard old-valid/new-invalid break under normal FHIR validation semantics because warning constraints do not make an instance invalid. It can still break warning-as-error build pipelines, generated artifact publication checks, or systems that use invariant keys in suppression lists.
findings.migrationGuidanceMd: Audit CompartmentDefinition `name` and `url` values before R6 publication. Update warning suppressions from `cpd-0` to `cnl-0` where necessary, and avoid `|`, `#`, and spaces in canonical URLs.
findings.backwardCompatibilityAnalysisMd: Because these are warnings, the design is mostly backward-compatible. The avoidable part is the changed invariant key and stricter regex, which can surprise automated tooling even when instance validation remains non-fatal.

findings.title: resource.param now explicitly means the core HL7 SearchParameter code, not a server alias

oldState.summary: R4 described `param` broadly as the name of a search parameter representing the link to the compartment.

semanticText.definition: The name of a search parameter that represents the link to the compartment. More than one may be listed because a resource may be linked to a compartment in more than one way,.
semanticText.comment: If no search parameters are listed, then the resource is not linked to the compartment.

oldState.narrativeMd: R4 did not explicitly distinguish the base HL7 SearchParameter code from a server-specific SearchParameter code.

newState.summary: R6 says `param` is the search parameter code as defined in the core specification and clarifies that server-specific aliases do not change compartment membership.

semanticText.definition: The search parameter 'code' as defined in the core specification that represents the link to the compartment.
semanticText.comment: More than one may be listed because a resource may be linked to a compartment in more than one way.  Note that a given server might use a different 'code' for the SearchParameter in their CapabilityStatement.  The inclusion rules are based on the 'base' HL7 search parameter code value, not the server-specific code value.  E.g. if a server uses code 'doc' instead of 'performer' for their Procedure performer search performer, the 'doc' search would still apply when determining membership in the Practitioner compartment. If no search parameters are listed, then the resource is not linked to the compartment.

newState.narrativeMd: The shape is unchanged, but the interpretation is stricter and more explicit: compartment inclusion is keyed to base HL7 search parameter codes.

facts.oldValue: The name of a search parameter that represents the link to the compartment.
facts.newValue: The search parameter 'code' as defined in the core specification that represents the link to the compartment.
Server-specific SearchParameter codes in CapabilityStatement do not change the base HL7 code used for compartment inclusion.

structuredDelta.matchingRationaleMd: The same element id/path/type/cardinality persists; only the normative descriptive text changes.

impact.impactRationaleMd: No JSON/XML instance becomes invalid from this text change alone. The risk is behavioral: implementations that computed compartment membership using local server SearchParameter aliases can produce different compartment membership than R6 expects. For compartments used in authorization or `$everything`, that is a high runtime migration risk.
impact.safetyOrBusinessRiskMd: Compartment membership commonly gates search results and access scopes. Alias-based interpretation can over-include or under-include resources.

justification.inferredGoal: Remove ambiguity about whether compartment rules use base HL7 search parameter codes or server-specific aliases.
justification.backwardCompatibleAlternativeSummary: Add first-class alias-mapping support while preserving broad R4 `param` wording.
justification.justificationRationaleMd: The goal of making compartment membership depend on stable core HL7 SearchParameter codes is interoperability- and safety-relevant. A compatibility design could preserve alias-based implementations, but that would undercut the clarification and risk inconsistent access-control or compartment-search results.
justification.backwardCompatibleAlternativeMd: A partial base-design alternative would keep `resource.param` broadly defined and add an optional alias-mapping element for server-specific SearchParameter codes. That is less disruptive for implementations that used local aliases, but it creates duplicate representations for the same relationship and leaves open which code governs membership when aliases conflict with base definitions.
justification.alternativeTradeoffSummary: Supporting both base codes and server aliases would ease migration but create ambiguity in compartment membership, authorization, and `$everything` behavior.

evidence.detail: R4 describes the element as the name of a search parameter and only says no parameters means not linked.
R6 says the value is the core specification search parameter code and gives an alias example (`doc` versus `performer`).

examples.examplesMd: The R6 comment itself gives the key example: if a server exposes a Procedure performer search with local code `doc`, the compartment rule still uses the base HL7 code `performer` for Practitioner-compartment membership.

findings.narrativeMd: This is a semantic break rather than a structural break. The same string array remains, but R6 tells implementers how to interpret the strings: they are the base HL7 SearchParameter codes, not arbitrary server-local names.
findings.validationAndCompatibilityMd: Instance validation does not change because the element remains `0..* string`. Runtime behavior can change if a server previously treated local CapabilityStatement SearchParameter codes as authoritative for compartment membership. This affects query planning, authorization filters, and `$everything` inclusion rules.
findings.migrationGuidanceMd: Review compartment-membership code for any use of server-specific SearchParameter aliases. Normalize `resource.param` values to the core HL7 code before evaluating membership, and add tests where local server codes differ from base codes. Access-control tests should include both alias and base-code paths.
findings.backwardCompatibilityAnalysisMd: The clarification may have been necessary for interoperable compartment behavior, but it could have been introduced with explicit alias-mapping support to ease migration for existing servers.
